title: Qt: Present language preference choices in native names
description:
Offer the language options in the native names of the languages instead
of always using English.

Instead of translating "Use system setting" with the current locale,
use the system locale, since that's more likely to be understood by
the user if the user has selected a different locale and is the language
that will be switched to if that option is selected. If the user can't
understand a translation to the system locale, then picking that option
isn't helpful.

Sort them before adding to the combo box, so that "Use system setting"
is always the first entry, instead of often being the last but sometimes
in the middle, depending on translation.

Since some languages using Latin script use uppercase for language names
(e.g., most Germanic languages) and others do not (e.g., most Romance
languages), sort case insensitively. Use the system locale for
collation, so that if the system locale is, e.g., Cyrillic script
all the native language names in Cyrillic script will be sorted first.

Connect the language QComboBox CurrentIndexChanged signal after the
initial setup, so that change the combobox to the current value of the
prefs doesn't trigger setting the pref to its current value. (That can
also cause more problems if the combobox entries are emptied, etc.)

Note that this does mean we list, e.g., "American English" instead of
just "English," but then again our English translation is American English.

Fix #19305

notes.body:
> Since some languages using Latin script use uppercase for language names (e.g., most Germanic languages) and others do not (e.g., most Romance languages), sort case insensitively.

At least on macOS, the selector for languages to add to the list of preferred languages lists "Català", "Español", "Français", "Galego", "Italiano", "Português", and "Românǎ", so it's using uppercase for several Romance languages, although it also lists "aragonés", so it's not *universally* using uppercase for them, and thus isn't even *sentence* case.

But, yes, without a consistent use of either sentence or title case, case-insensitive sorting is the right thing to do.

Or is this a question of the *system*/*current* language setting, e.g. "if the system language is a Romance language, language names do not use initial caps, but if it's a Germanic language, they do (except, apparently, for Aragonese and Abkhazian in macOS with English as the Germanic language in question)?

For locales, Qt provides a "give me the name of this language in English, regardless of my current locale" static function, and a "give me the native name of this locale's language" member function.

It does not, unfortunately, provide a "give me the native name of some other locale's language, but capitalized according to the rules of my current or system locale." It also does not provide a "give me the name of this other locale's language, translated into my locale," though that might be possible with the translate function. We probably don't want to do the latter anyway, though, since people probably want to change the language when the current locale isn't preferred.

So as a result (as also seen in a comment in #19305), when using the "native name" function one gets "English" but "français." We could, however, just run the results through `str.replace(0, 1, str.at(0).toUpper());` and assume that even in, e.g., a French locale that looks better and more professional. Perhaps one of our native French speakers has an opinion?

It would be the first (sometimes only) word in the item so capitalizing is probably ok regardless of locale, I guess.

@alagoutte @pquantin any opinions?
I didn't switch my Mac to "make French the system language" and then get the list of languages; I'll try that on one of my VMs.

> I didn't switch my Mac to "make French the system language" and then get the list of languages; I'll try that on one of my VMs.

For what it's worth, on my Tahoe VM, I switched the preferred language to French, quit and restarted System Settings so that it got the new language (I was surprised that it didn't just get a "system preferred language changed" indication and update...), and now Réglages Système shows the language list with French rather than English descriptions following the in-their-own-writ names, but still spells "Français" with a capital "F".

So I guess Qt uses different conventions from macOS. (I haven't checked Windows or GNOME VMs.)

It may be that Qt is not capitalizing them, but Qt might consider it reasonable to capitalize the names when they are the first word of a dropdown. That's an easy enough change, if done for all locales. (Just as easy would be "always lowercase," whereas "uppercase or lowercase them all depending on the current or system locale" I'm not sure we have the comprehensive rules for.)
KDE appears to, regardless of locale, take what Qt's `nativeLanguageName` returns and capitalize the first letter in the combobox. So that is looking like a popular and reasonable choice.
